summary: Defines physics forces for solvers: continuous Bullet linear/torque forces, Bullet impulse-style usage through related impulse controls, and Flex spherical force fields.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Enables the continuous active force or force field

key_params.name: relpos
key_params.note: Application point relative to the physical center of the body

key_params.name: falloff
key_params.note: Controls force-field strength decay across the radius

key_concepts: Force COMP adds physics forces to Bullet simulations and spherical force fields to NVIDIA Flex simulations.
Active Bullet forces apply over time each frame, either globally through Bullet Solver COMP or locally through Actor COMP.
Force and Torque values are in Newtons, so actor mass affects acceleration from the same force value.
Relative Position applies linear force away from the physical center and can introduce rotation through added torque.
Force Field mode is spherical: positive Strength pushes bodies outward, negative Strength pulls inward, and Radius/Falloff shape the field.
common_gotchas: A Bullet Force COMP must be referenced by a Bullet Solver COMP for global force, or by an Actor COMP for local force.
Active force is applied over time each frame, while impulse force behavior changes velocity instantly for one frame.
Force values are in Newtons; mass changes acceleration, so equal forces move lighter actors more quickly.
A non-zero Relative Position can add torque and cause rotation even when the force vector is linear.
For per-body force/torque control, use feedback channels on Actor COMP or Bullet Solver COMP.
Flex force fields are spherical; positive strength pushes outward and negative strength pulls inward.
